summary: This June 20, 2026 Dante livestream is high-pressure Paradiso accounting: it already links several strong marks to Guide Trap, Fictional Heroes, Poetry, and Human Heart, while adding held seed pressure around Heaven as remembered bliss, imagination beyond love, anti-authority self-questioning, and active human participation in redemption.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The poem is memorized before it is fully understood, implanted like operating software, and unlocked slowly by life.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Poetry page already owns the poem-as-invasion mechanism; this source gives a sharper operating-software formulation without requiring a new public page.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Love holds people together across distance and dimensions, but it must be between persons rather than God, money, or an abstraction.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Love Recognizes The Other owns love as concrete personal recognition. Human Heart owns the broader civilizational measure; Poetry owns the medium that carries love outward.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Poetry is love's fullest expression because it gives love form, recruits others into it, and carries it across time and space.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This is Poetry rather than a generic love topic because the active mechanism is language making private love communicable and durable.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Beatrice gets Dante to the threshold, but the beloved cannot hold him through the final act; he must go on without being held.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Guide Trap owns necessary mediation that must be outgrown. This source extends the pattern beyond Virgil to Beatrice/Bernard without making Beatrice a trap in the same sense as Virgil.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Paradise has to come first because otherwise readers mistake Virgil's explanations for Dante's own vision; Virgil is necessary but unreliable.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Fictional Heroes owns Virgil as an interior literary presence the reader must defeat; Guide Trap owns the trusted mediation problem.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use in a future Dante/Poetry replacement pass: the Divine Comedy works like operating software, a seed, and music for memory. It is memorized before it is understood, keeps generating meaning over decades, and triggers the reader's own happiest memories so Paradise can be felt rather than merely reported.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry owns the medium: memory, rhythm, imagination, shared language, and love made durable. Stories owns broader narrative world-setting; Eschatology owns heaven/death as final-order script.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold for a Guide Trap replacement/compression pass, not an ordinary append: this source distinguishes necessary guidance from final truth twice. Beatrice can raise Dante to the threshold but must yield to imagination, while Virgil can begin the journey but must be recognized as unreliable after Paradise reveals the true destination.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Guide Trap owns threshold mediation and the need to outgrow a guide. Fictional Heroes owns Virgil as interiorized literary character; Human Heart/Love owns concrete beloved relation.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use as additional support for the Virgil interior-guide anchor: Jiang says the course must read Paradise before Inferno so readers do not confuse Virgil's world with Dante's own, and he frames Dante's deeper war as displacing Virgil as the poet who still governs the inherited universe.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Fictional Heroes owns the character living inside the reader. Guide Trap owns the guide's mediation; Poetry owns the civilizational medium that lets Virgil remain active.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this source when revising the personal-eschatology section: Heaven is defined experientially as the happiest second stretched forever, reconstructed through emotion and memory; fear of death is a control mechanism that Dante counters by making the afterlife imaginatively inhabitable and loving rather than merely terrifying.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Eschatology owns heaven, death, fear, and the afterlife as lived script. Poetry owns the technique that triggers memory; Human Heart owns relation and concrete love.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only in a future agency-focused Dante pass: Jiang reads Mary, faith, imagination, and redemption as active rather than passive. People are not saved by waiting to be managed from above; they exercise faith and imagination in a way that makes redemption possible.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Free Will owns active participation, faith, agency, and refusal of passive salvation. Eschatology owns the heaven/redemption frame; Poetry owns Dante's reordering of the official world.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the children's-poem and Beatrice sections as Human Heart support: love is concrete relation across distance and dimensions, and Jiang's own happiest memory is simply his children. Do not append ordinary prose unless Human Heart is being compressed or its Dante/Love chronology is being revised.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Human Heart owns relation, children, love, connection, and community as the center of meaning. Poetry owns the expression of that relation across time and space.

new_lens_seeds.title: Heaven As Remembered Bliss
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Heaven becomes intelligible through emotion and memory rather than visual possession: the happiest second, release, homecoming, recognition, beauty, children, and love are stretched into an afterlife that poetry can make readers feel.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare Paradiso, fear of death, memory, poetry, love, and body-based imagination without becoming a generic Heaven topic. It explains how Jiang moves from ordinary human scenes into eschatology.
new_lens_seeds.reason: Hold as a seed until compared against earlier Paradiso, cave/death, and eschatology sources. The current public pages can route the components without a standalone Heaven page.

new_lens_seeds.title: Imagination Beyond Love
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: A beloved or guide can bring the person to the threshold, but the final act requires imagination, ego, expression, and active selfhood rather than complete dissolution into the beloved.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: This explains Beatrice yielding to Bernard, poetry as love's highest expression, and the body's role in seeing God. It may later clarify boundaries among Love, Guide Trap, Poetry, Free Will, and Eschatology.
new_lens_seeds.reason: Hold as a boundary-review seed. It is powerful, but immediate public promotion would blur Love, Guide Trap, Poetry, and Free Will without a concept-scoped comparison.

new_lens_seeds.title: Dante's Anti-Authority Self-Questioning
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Dante can hide rebellion inside orthodoxy so the reader is trained to question Peter, church, poet, teacher, and self rather than settle into a pious answer key.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The source gives a compact method for how canonical form can smuggle self-subversion past gatekeepers, but it currently overlaps Poetry, Stories, Free Will, and Legitimacy Fiction.
new_lens_seeds.reason: Hold as a method seed. The immediate action is routing to Poetry/Stories/Free Will, not a standalone Peter, Coin, or Anti-Church page.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-06-20, this lecture sits after the June 15-18 Paradiso sources and one day before the June 21 Inferno/Dis seminar. It should be treated as the Paradise-first explanation for why Virgil must later be read as necessary but unreliable, while the June 21 source supplies the later Dis jurisdiction layer.

This source gives a June 20 Paradiso formulation where Heaven is felt through emotion, memory, and bliss, and Dante's public act is to loosen institutional fear of death. Later public eschatology work should preserve that personal-experiential layer alongside geopolitical end-times scripts.

The lecture intensifies the Dante love trail by grounding Beatrice and poetry in concrete human relation: a father's distant children, Jiang's own children, and love as connection across dimensions. This should be compared with earlier Beatrice and Love Recognizes The Other evidence before any public chronology rewrite.

next_actions.note: Do not append this source mechanically to Guide Trap, Poetry, Human Heart, or Eschatology. Poetry is around 5.4k words and Human Heart around 5.1k words; future public work should be replacement/compression or a concept-scoped boundary review.
